tools.name: search_procedures

A positive Node --max-old-space-size, including NODE_OPTIONS, overrides that request and is not limited by the setting's floor or maximum. A heap failure names the effective request, its source (default or setting), the default, the floor, and the maximum. Select detail summary for counts and retained native-inventory pages; complete remains the default.

tools.description: Write provider pseudocode for every analyzed function, or a filtered subset, into a caller-selected directory and return only a manifest. Each file records the provider function name, canonical address, inclusive body ranges when procedure_info supplies them, and that function's procedure_info and pseudocode limitations. Each function's index record keeps its latest attempt and its complete limitations; the journal keeps earlier attempts and their limitations. Evidence keeps at most eight first-observed distinct per-function limitations within an encoded-text budget; the omitted count measures observations, not distinct warnings. The manifest reports counts, the output directory, the index path, at most 32 failure details within 2,048 JSON-encoded UTF-8 bytes (names can be omitted; full names remain in the index), provider identity, and the analysis-profile digest. Pseudocode stays in the files. An existing directory is refused unless resume is set and the journal matches the target SHA-256, provider, and analysis profile; verified files are skipped and conflicting files are left unchanged. layout dwarf reports that compilation-unit paths are unavailable and names files by address. Set retry_failed: independent_fresh to retry a null result explicitly reported as a function failure when supported; the failed attempt stays in the journal and the new attempt may use different analysis context. Errors and omissions without that typed fact are not retried. A failure of one function does not stop the others. Functions procedure_info classifies as external are counted as external, get no file, and are not decompiled; a resume skips them. Cancellation leaves files already written. Per-function limits do not bound the whole call; use limit and resume to select work that fits the client deadline, including import, listing and file work.

inputs.name: resume

Verified files and functions recorded as external are skipped, conflicting files are left unchanged, and functions not yet tried run before retries of recorded failures.

tools.name: inspect_analysis_view
tools.description: Use native-procedure-references to page retained procedure reference or unresolved-call rows. Endpoint kind selected-procedure refers to the summary procedure, null preserves the original null, and shared carries an index into items.endpoints, where each other procedure is stored once per page. Exact source_address and target_address filters apply to reference rows. For inspect_api_contract parents, graphql-contract pages retained SDL types/fields, operation definitions, field references, fragment-spreads or diagnostics with exact filters and selected columns. Use javascript-routes collections to query route patterns, source-linked occurrences, source status, unknowns or summary counts from retained JavaScript application or web-bundle Evidence. Use web-bundle collections endpoints or inferences to page endpoint observations and inferences from retained analyze_web_bundle Evidence; summary returns target URL, origin, and counts. For retained trace_feature Evidence, kind native-feature-trace pages matches, references or unknowns; matches filter exact address, references filter exact source_address and target_address, source_index identifies each original row, and list_unknowns pages durable question heads. Inspect selected views of supported completed Evidence without repeating analysis. Use recorded-array with an exact raw_result object-member path to page a provider-recorded array when the producer supplies that path; rows keep their raw meaning and the parent retains coverage. For procedure_pseudo_code Evidence, summary reports text availability and the original selection; kind native with facet pseudocode pages the original UTF-16 text. Other native facets require analyze_function. Choose a view compatible with the parent operation described below. Command summary views preserve ordered GDB records or opaque objdump stdout/stderr once, source parameters, completion facts and parent identity. They do not establish current target state. Historical capture summaries return identity and counts without bodies or archive inventories. Capture views page retained records: view {kind: "capture", detail: "preview" | "complete", offset: 0, limit: 20}; preview selects recorded headline fields and binary descriptors, complete returns exact records with all sidecars. Offsets follow the selected parent record order, preserving original producer ordinals. Paging never reopens the source or reruns the decoder. Native export tables use kind native-exports, collection exports/issues, exact names or original indices, selected fields and matching-row pagination; parent Evidence plus source_index identifies each row. Source coverage stays separate from page coverage. BEAM views use kind beam, collections atoms/exports/imports/lambdas/chunks, exact names/indices/fields and matching-row pages; import modules intersects function names. source_index identifies original parent-and-collection rows, preserving every arity and raw atom index. beam.counts preserves null missing tables versus decoded empty tables; runtime absence remains unknown. PYC views use kind python-pyc, collection code_objects, names/indices/fields and paging; source_index scopes every same-name alternative to the parent, nested_code keeps code-constant references, and pyc.coverage preserves source coverage. Go metadata uses kind go, collection dependencies/settings, exact paths/keys or indices, fields and pagination. Row index refers to the original collection; empty selections return no rows, and dependency coverage remains unknown. Rust metadata uses kind rust, collection packages/edges, exact names/versions or original indices, selected fields, edge from_indices/to_indices and matching-row pagination. Embedded-record coverage is separate from unknown runtime dependencies. For inspect_pcap_capture parents, kind pcap pages endpoints, dns-queries, tls-sni, protocols, http-uris or unattributed-addresses. Select an exact query for dns-addresses, or a tshark/capinfos stream for UTF-16 diagnostics text. Page totals count retained facts; source coverage remains explicit. Qlog summaries keep profile/scope and counts; kind qlog pages traces, streams, loss-declarations, incomplete-records, contributions, ranges or final-sizes. Except traces, select trace_index; stream-specific facets also require exact stream_id and direction. Facts retain all-recorded-events-before-selection scope, and interval overlap or endpoint loss declarations do not prove retransmission or network loss. The api-surface view groups retained HAR requests by method, origin and format-rule path template; templated segments are inferences. It reads no headers or bodies and reports no query values. The environment-manifest view projects the same HAR requests on the primary origin (most JSON-like records) into a replayable tool surface: view {kind: "environment-manifest", template_rules: ["after-uid-literal", "opaque-token", "sibling-variance"], include_query_parameter_names: true}. Each tool has a deterministic name, a path template and parameters from the four format rules plus the selected opt-in rules, observed query parameter names, a value-free body shape for POST/PUT/PATCH, status and content-type sets and record ordinals; records are pointers into the parent, excluded groups carry a reason and three fixed unknowns are always stated. Templates, parameters and names are inferences; the view copies no header, cookie or body values and refuses parents inspected with sensitive values. A capture_browser_scenario parent also supports summary and browser-scenario steps/events/transactions/text pages, preserving step_indices, event_kinds, transaction_ids and selected artifacts. A capture_browser_scenario parent that selected response bodies or header values projects the same way, one record per network transaction in request order; it relies on capture-time redaction of declared secrets instead of that refusal, and a transaction whose URL was redacted is left unrepresented. The environment-state view extracts, from the same parents, the initial state the recorded reads observed: view {kind: "environment-state", template_rules: [...]} with the rules of the manifest it accompanies. It reads response bodies recorded before the first related write and reports entity types with an identity field (proved by a path parameter or inferred from a field name), entities in collection order with per-view values where views differ, documents for non-parameterized reads that are not entities and have one initial request line (item-shaped paths stay recorded), and a render plan per read tool: item and list views reproduce their latest recordings from the state (a list also learns the filters, search, sort and paging its recordings verify, and answers new values of them from the state), and every other read tool is a recorded view with a reason. It also reports a write plan per state-changing tool (create, update, delete or document, built from its first successful call) and write_clock; a plan is served only when replaying the capture shows a later read confirming its effect and none contradicting it. Types and identity are inferences; values are recorded data, so it refuses parents inspected with sensitive values, and a scenario parent must have selected response bodies; its values keep the capture redaction markers, and a write whose URL it redacted ends the state of every type. The environment-coverage view, view {kind: "environment-coverage", template_rules: [...]}, summarizes that state without its entities: reads.state and reads.recorded count read tools answered from the state and replayed (recorded_reasons per view reason), writes.served lists the served write tools, and writes.withheld lists each other write tool with its reason, plan record, contradicting read and a hint about what to record next; it refuses what the environment-state view refuses. For a retained record use source: {kind: "retained-evidence", evidence_id: "<parent_evidence_id>"}. Use normalized_result.parent_evidence_id from a summary receipt. Source kind is required. Portable source uses {kind: "inline", evidence: <complete Evidence>}. A completed Evidence JSON file on this host uses {kind: "evidence-file", path: "<absolute path>"}: REA reads and authenticates it, then projects it like retained Evidence, so a large capture is bounded by the file reader rather than by inline-input accounting. The file may also be an Evidence bundle written by CLI --evidence_output or export_evidence_bundle; select evidence_id when it contains more than one record. For layout, JavaScript, inventory, WASM, Mach-O, Interface Builder, EVM, managed artifact, Android package and Dart AOT sources, request a summary with view: {kind: "summary"}; summary is a view kind and has no facet. The WASM summary gives validation, counts, WAT digest/length, tool profile and execution/network states without reading WAT text. Select a layout mitigations/linkage facet, one section/symbol/module, or a stable page. Module pages include assets, bundled and source modules; exported symbol bindings are not module units and stay out of them. use node_id for ambiguous or unavailable paths. Typed module references use view {kind: "javascript", collection: "modules", projection: "references", where: {path: "main.js", kind: "javascript-module"}, offset: 0, limit: 64}; where matches exact retained strings (null selects unavailable paths). Rows include canonical identity, retained source-range count and observation support states. Source coverage and selection remain explicit; exhausting matching rows does not prove runtime loading or complete analysis. For exact file/native facts and processing gaps, use view {kind: "javascript-facts", where: {paths: ["package.json"]}, property_keys: ["name", "operation", "analysis_status"]}. Rows page original observations with canonical identities and Evidence; missing properties remain omitted. Paths match recorded artifact-path/source-range locations; optional kinds filter nodes. To discover field names without values, opt into include_available_property_keys: true with property_keys: []. Canonical identity and Evidence are separate from properties; keep each node_id/observation_id pair together when composing results. Inventory uses view: {kind: "inventory", collection: "occurrences", logical_paths: ["package.json"], offset: 0, limit: 64}. Inventory views page nodes, occurrences, edges or integrity contradictions. Occurrences accept exact logical_paths and occurrence_ids; nodes accept artifact_ids. Batch filters intersect (omitted means all available, [] means none); fields selects columns while retaining identity links. source_complete describes retained graph membership; source_coverage describes producer coverage, including unknown encrypted PCK directories. Page exhaustion does not prove absence in a partial source. WASM views use kind wasm and facet sections/imports/exports/candidates/glue/wat/headers/details/tool_profile; text facets use UTF-16 code units and source forms remain exact. Mach-O views use kind macho and facet entrypoints/architectures/build_metadata/load_commands/dependencies/imports/exports/segments/provenance; source_exhaustive false means unreturned rows may exist. Interface Builder views use kind interface-builder and collection documents/nodes/edges/coverage; nodes and edges accept an exact document relative_path. EVM summary returns all inferred interface candidates, carrier/decoded identities and explicit unknowns without hex or duplicate stdout. EVM views use kind evm and facet functions/bytecode_hex/stdout/stderr; function pages preserve the original candidate rows, and text offsets/limits count UTF-16 code units (hex has two characters per decoded byte). Exhausting candidate pages does not establish global interface completeness. Managed artifact summaries preserve complete identity/classification, metadata status, module/MVID, frameworks, coverage and limitations without unrelated inventories. Managed pages use kind managed and collection references/resources/attributes, retaining source coverage and build-local token scope; page exhaustion does not establish complete metadata. Managed member summaries keep identity, selection with unmatched names, coverage and per-collection counts; managed-members pages use collection types/exported_types/fields/methods/member_refs/call_edges/field_accesses/user_strings. Exact names and declaring_types filters intersect before paging where supported; fields selects columns (distinct from collection: "fields"). Identity/source_index, module MVID, source coverage and unresolved filter counts remain; omit body to avoid IL anchors. Omitted fields preserves full rows. Android package summaries retain all declarations, engine identity and counts without decoded manifest text. Android manifest pages use kind android, facet manifest, offset and limit in UTF-16 code units; source_status preserves partial decoded coverage even when the retained text page is exhausted. Dart AOT summary preserves target/ABI/library identity, snapshot headers and pool lower bounds. String pages use kind dart-aot, collection package_uris/dart_uris/class_like_tokens; source coverage remains partial when the producer says partial. Protobuf views use kind protobuf, collection bodies/frames/fields, with record_ordinals, body_pointers and fields; field pages also select frame_indices, field_ids, field_numbers or schema_names. Byte identity, offset basis and body status remain present. Text and schema_value are opt-in page columns. APK signing views use kind apk-signature and collection signers/digests/lineage, with ids, signer_ids, schemes, fields and paging. Identity links remain when fields is empty. Declared identities and digest matches do not establish signature verification or authenticity. Model views use kind model-artifact and collection metadata (keys), tensors (names/types) or types (derived totals), with indices, fields and paging. Header SHA-256 scopes declarations; full-file identity remains unknown unless full hashing was selected. Arrays retain typed eight-element previews with explicit omissions. IL2CPP metadata views use kind il2cpp-metadata and collection sections/images/types/methods/fields/properties/events/parameters/string_literals/code_gen_modules/method_addresses/return_types/field_types/parameter_types/generic_method_instances/generic_method_issues. Select indices, fields and pages; sections/images/types/methods/fields/properties/events/parameters/return_types/field_types/parameter_types/generic_method_instances accept exact names (native type names match retained rendered values, preserving same-name rows; null names never match), types also accept image_indices/namespaces/declaring_types, and methods/members accept declaring_types. Parameters and parameter_types accept method_indices; code_gen_modules accept image_indices; method_addresses and generic_method_instances accept addresses/states (generic_method_instances also method_indices), preserving every folded alternative; generic_method_issues accept rows. Row index is scoped to the metadata digest; native pages add binary_source. Uncollected native tables have null counts and remain unavailable. Desktop directory views use kind desktop-application and collection files/omissions/candidates/components/next_probes, with fields and pagination; files and omissions accept exact paths or their stable IDs, and candidates accept families. Source coverage and stable row IDs remain available. Native load-image Evidence uses kind native-load-image with collection source_files/mappings/relocations/entry_points/entry_context/checks/sections, original indices, collection-specific fields and offset/limit paging. Null collections remain unrecorded or inapplicable; pages preserve unsupported verification. Native inventory Evidence from list_names, list/search_procedures or list/search_strings uses view: {kind: "native-inventory", offset: 0, limit: 64, fields: ["value"]}. Rows keep source_index and address even with selected fields. Summary counts describe retained rows; provider discovery coverage remains unknown. Native function Evidence accepts kind summary for identity, availability and facet counts, or kind native for selected facts: view: {kind: "native", facet: "procedure"}. Facets select procedure, pseudocode, assembly, basic blocks, comments, callers/callees, references, unresolved calls, referenced strings/names, native_api and value-flow observations. For parameter type paths when value flow is recorded, use facet: "value_flow_parameters"; its decompiler-observed path may be passed to inspect_native_data_type, but exact database lookup can be unavailable and does not by itself establish type identity. Use nonnegative offset and a positive caller-selected limit (defaults 0 and 64); pseudocode uses UTF-16 code units, other native pages use rows. Retained batch_decompile Evidence accepts kind summary for counts and sizes, or view: {kind: "batch-decompile", collection: "items", where: {statuses: ["unavailable", "error"]}} for body-free rows with exact indices, addresses, procedure_addresses or statuses (include_pseudocode adds bodies), or collection "pseudocode" with an index to page one body. Returns artifact identity, parent Evidence ID, a distinct view digest, coverage, limitations and unknowns. Actual serialized size determines MCP transport admission; choose a smaller page or export the complete retained Evidence if needed.

tools.name: inspect_artifact
tools.description: Inspect an active archive, application package, firmware container (including FIT and legacy uImage), Node.js SEA carrier, or Deno compile executable in one call. By default returns the complete content-addressed artifact graph once, as the typed nested inventory Evidence, with root and integrity observations, integrity contradictions, hypotheses, unexplored branches, limitations, and next probes inline. Bun standalone inventory describes stored module, sourcemap and opaque bytecode regions. Deno compile inventory reports the embedded virtual filesystem, remote modules, and recorded options. Environment-file values and certificate bytes are retained in local Evidence with their counts and byte lengths. The npm snapshot length is reported and not decoded, and the executable is not run. For PCK, Bun and large containers prefer detail summary: it retains the complete inspection and returns its derived summary view; read exact paths, batch occurrence/content IDs and selected fields with inspect_analysis_view using parent_evidence_id. This changes delivery, not inventory coverage. Classic iNES includes header facts, PRG/CHR file-region hashes and byte-exact reconstruction evidence; mapper execution and CPU bank mappings remain unobserved. Read-only DMG mounting is used automatically on supported macOS hosts. Integrity mismatches fail by default; record-and-continue keeps mismatches explicitly untrusted. It does not extract files; use extract_artifact to materialize regular contents of supported formats. DMG extraction is unavailable; use a caller-managed read-only mount on macOS to access its files.

Expands @executable_path, @loader_path, and @rpath through each process's LC_RPATH stack in dependents-first load order, and reports every candidate path with its outcome, the resolved image and digest, weak, re-export, upward, and lazy-load flags, including LC_LAZY_LOAD_DYLIB_INFO linkedit payloads, and derived findings such as unresolved required loads or absent earlier @rpath candidates. No target execution, extraction, network or target changes. tools.name: inspect_evm_interface
tools.description: Inspect explicit local flat EVM bytecode without target execution or chain/RPC access. Select raw or hex encoding explicitly. For all inferred selectors/offsets/arguments/mutability and identities without bytecode hex or duplicated stdout, select detail: "summary" on this first call: it retains unchanged complete Evidence and returns a distinct linked inspect_analysis_view summary. Read original function rows or bytecode_hex/stdout/stderr text pages using view kind evm and normalized_result.parent_evidence_id; original complete Evidence remains accessible. Bytecode kind, hardfork, deployed authenticity and discovery completeness stay unknown; summary coverage covers only producer-returned candidates. Unchanged bundled EVMole 0.9.3/WASM in an owned bounded worker is initially real-verified on Linux x64; EOF-style EF00 containers are unsupported. Adjust timeout_ms (default 30000 ms, integer 1..2147483647) for the owned worker command on the next call; omitted timeout_ms keeps 30000 ms. inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Absolute path to caller-selected local bytecode carrier

inputs.name: encoding

tools.name: inspect_web_network_capture
tools.description: Explicit record_ordinals also decode retained protobuf/gRPC bodies whose declared content type is recognized. Optional protobuf selects exact body_pointers, framing, and a caller-supplied local FileDescriptorSet with message_type. Native gRPC and gRPC-web framing remain distinct. Wire fields are flat byte-range facts; ambiguous readings stay candidates, compressed payloads stay unknown. Page retained decoding with inspect_analysis_view kind protobuf, collection bodies/frames/fields, exact batch selectors and fields. Large text and schema values require explicit fields selection in those pages. Request detail summary for capture identity and counts; then page retained records with inspect_analysis_view kind capture (preview or complete), avoiding repeated decoding. Default detail complete preserves existing inline delivery. Inspect retained local HAR 1.2, native mitmproxy, Fiddler SAZ or aioquic 1.5.0 JSON qlog 0.3 events without contacting recorded URLs. Qlog reports trace-scoped STREAM interval unions and endpoint loss declarations; it does not recover bodies, prove network loss or correlate PCAP. Other qlog layouts are unsupported. Uses pinned upstream parsers, owned temporary files and bounded offline processes. SAZ preserves HTTP fields, XML metadata and encoded body/message bytes without replay or HAR conversion; encrypted archives are unsupported. Native mitmproxy requires caller-supplied mitmdump 12.2.3 on Linux. Browser transaction IDs, runtime attribution and original bytes of HAR Unicode text remain unknown.

tools.name: start_build_computer
tools.description: Start a local agentenv computer to build a desktop app environment on, and return its id with a first screenshot as an image. From a request, REA renders a bundle that installs the app from the Ubuntu archive, an apt repository or a .deb URL, opens it on demand from its desktop entry (it is not open at first: start_build_capture opens it under capture, and only when no capture is under way is it opened from the desktop's Applications menu, under Other, by the environment's name), and installs REA itself in a build-only layer from REA_BUILD_COMPUTER_REA_ARCHIVE. Set source.electron for an Electron app: the install rewrites that desktop entry's command with the same launch policy an export uses, adding --no-sandbox right after the program unless the command already has it, because the container does not grant the user namespaces Chromium needs and Electron exits without the flag. From a bundle folder, such as an exported one, it starts that bundle's smoke task as it is. Needs Docker and the agentenv runner named by REA_AGENT_ENV_COMMAND; the first start of a bundle builds its image, which downloads packages and can take minutes, and agentenv makes a start wait while another agentenv run on this host writes its bundle's ids, so starts at the same time can wait minutes for each other. screenshot sets the first screenshot's region, format and quality. The computer stays up, reachable on this host, until close_build_computer or the server closes; when a start fails before its teardown is confirmed, the error's computer_id names what close_build_computer retries.

tools.name: act_on_build_computer
tools.description: Drive the app on a build computer: one action, screenshot, click, drag, scroll, type, type_secret, key, wait, reset. Each but reset and type_secret is sent to the computer's computer_<action> tool with the fields given, which are the driver's own arguments; type_secret types into the focused field the value of the secret its handle names, a file the person wrote in REA's build-secrets folder on this host ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/rea/build-secrets/<handle>, or ~/.config/rea/build-secrets/<handle>), readable only by them: no result, log or record shows the value, only the handle, so it takes no screenshot, and the field must be one that masks what is typed, since a later screenshot shows the screen; reset restores the app's data to its seed with data/reset, which relaunches the app, and returns once the computer is ready again; a screenshot asked of it that then fails leaves the reset done, its result naming why in screenshot_error. Points are pixels of the latest frame, so take a screenshot first, or space norm on a 0..norm_scale grid; count 2 double-clicks; a drag's path takes 2 to 50 points; a screenshot with region does not capture the screen again, it crops the latest frame, so take a full screenshot, or a wait with screenshot true, first; keys names one chord in W3C names, and spellings such as ctrl+s are translated. Returns the driver's content unchanged, its images included, and its structured result; an action's screenshot is taken at once, so after one that opens a menu or a window, take it with a wait instead; a refusal, such as a stale frame, is an error with the computer's message. Each action is logged on the computer. Actions, capture steps and checks on one computer run one at a time, in the order they arrive; computers run side by side.

inputs.name: action

inputs.name: count
inputs.description: click: 2 double-clicks.

inputs.name: modifiers
inputs.description: Keys held during a click, drag or scroll.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: drag: 2 to 50 [x, y] points from press to release; the driver refuses more.

inputs.name: amount
inputs.description: scroll: notches.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: type: \n presses Enter, \t Tab.

inputs.name: secret
inputs.description: type_secret: the handle of a secret, the name of a file the person wrote in REA's build-secrets folder on this host; REA types its value, which no result shows.

inputs.name: keys
inputs.description: key: one chord pressed in order, as ["Control", "s"] or ["ctrl+s"].

inputs.name: ms
inputs.description: wait: milliseconds.

inputs.description: screenshot: [x0, y0, x1, y1] to crop to. It does not capture the screen again; it crops the latest frame, so take a full screenshot, or a wait with screenshot true, first.

inputs.name: quality
inputs.description: jpeg quality.

inputs.name: screenshot
inputs.description: Return a screenshot taken after the action.

tools.name: start_build_capture
tools.description: Begin REA's capture of the app on a build computer started from a request, inside the computer: REA downloads the package lists as the computer's user so the capture finds the app's sources, launches the app from its desktop entry under capture (do not open it from the menu first) and returns once its window is open, with a screenshot. When the app exits before its window opens, the error gives its exit code and the end of its stderr, with the capture's record of the session in its details. REA counts a file as the app's document when an app window's title shows its name or ~/ path; name the file the app will save in state_paths when its title shows something else, such as a score's title. Then make the seed through the app and save it, mark_build_checkpoint seed, make the change the task asks for and save it, mark_build_checkpoint end, and stop_build_capture.

inputs.name: computer_id
inputs.description: The id start_build_computer returned.

inputs.name: arguments
inputs.description: Arguments appended to the app's launch command, such as a file to open.

inputs.name: state_paths
inputs.description: Files or folders in the computer's home that hold the app's state, relative to the home (Documents/Scores/song.mscz), after ~/ or absolute under it; they need not exist yet. The capture retains them from its start and counts their files as the app's: a document, which the bundle owns, seeds and open

tools.name: mark_build_checkpoint
tools.description: Take a named checkpoint of the app's state in the capture under way and wait for the capture to acknowledge it, with its counts (entries walked, paths changed since the checkpoint before, files retained) and up to 10 of the files that changed, those a window title named first, then those under state_paths and those the app held open, caches last, so you can see which file a save wrote. Mark seed once the seed is saved and end once the change is; a name already taken is refused.

inputs.name: computer_id
inputs.description: The id start_build_computer returned.

inputs.name: name
inputs.description: Lowercase letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore. Name the seed seed and the end end: the draft and the export read them.

tools.name: stop_build_capture
tools.description: Stop the capture: the app is closed and the capture finishes inside the computer. Returns its checkpoints, the package and sources it found, its limitations and, when seed and end were marked and this server has not used a declared secret, the task draft between them: the files that changed under the paths the bundle owns, each with its net change and, for XML files, archives, JSON and key files, the values it added, changed and removed (before and after, at the pointers a check names them by); suggested checks; and guards, optional checks that the rest stays as it was. Notes say why a draft is empty (nothing changed; the changes lie outside the owned paths, listed with their roles; the app saved its change only in dconf, which no check reads; a dconf database changed that REA could not read; or REA recognized no document: capture again with state_paths naming the file, or make a change the app saves in a file) or why a file's suggestions are thin (only position names the change, it is all view state, its text is too long, or its view is cut or unreadable). If the server has used a declared secret, automatic drafting is withheld before it runs; write the task manually and give it to export_build_environment. Otherwise write the task from the draft, its prompt in the user's words.

inputs.name: computer_id
inputs.description: The id start_build_computer returned.

tools.name: export_build_environment
tools.description: Export the stopped capture as an agentenv computer app bundle with the given task, inside the computer, seeded at seed and checked at end, then copy the bundle to a new or empty folder on this host, every file checked against its digest. A bundle whose file names or contents hold a secret from REA's build-secrets folder, as it is, in UTF-16, hex, base64, URL encoding or inside a gzip file, is refused and written nowhere, the error naming the secrets' handles and the files. Files under the owned paths that changed between the pre-sign-in and post-sign-in checkpoints, and those named in withhold, are withheld from the seed as sign-in or licence state: each becomes a secret setting the deploy takes from an environment variable as the file's bytes in base64, the README says how to fill it, a check may not name it, and REA keeps its bytes as the secret withheld_files names by handle, for start_build_computer's settings when witnessing; a file larger than 48 KiB cannot be withheld. With seed_sign_in, they are seeded instead, which needs a seed_sign_in consent from record_build_consent; every recorded consent ships as consent.json. A task the export refuses, such as a check that already passes on the seed, is an error naming why. Witness the bundle next: start_build_computer from the folder and check_build_task.

inputs.name: computer_id
inputs.description: The id start_build_computer returned.

inputs.name: directory
inputs.description: A new or empty folder on this host for the bundle.

inputs.name: name
inputs.description: The environment's name; derived from the app by default.

inputs.name: withhold
inputs.description: Files under the owned paths to withhold from the seed as sign-in or licence state beside those the sign-in checkpoints find, such as a trial's licence file the app writes at first launch; relative to the home.

inputs.name: seed_sign_in
inputs.description: Seed the withheld files after all; needs a seed_sign_in consent from record_build_consent on this computer.

tools.name: check_build_task
tools.description: Grade a task's checks against the app's live state on a computer of an exported bundle: REA reads the app's data/get views and evaluates each check as the bundle's verifier does, one result per check, once the app's files settle (a screen_judge task instead takes a screenshot and runs the bundle's own judge on it with the agentenv runner's Python and model endpoint, three votes a question): it reads data/get every 0.5 s and grades once every file has held for 3 s, counted from the read that returned its bytes, so an app that saves a few seconds after the last key is graded on what it saved; no read begins 15 s or more after the first one began, one still in flight then is cut (read_cut), and files still changing are graded on the last completed read, with settled false. With stage, the check is part of the witness, in order: seed (give directory; REA begins recording) must fail a check, and on a computer started from a bundle folder it refuses a task whose steps and verifier in the bundle differ from what the export writes for it; after_edit, after acting on the app from the task's prompt alone, must pass every check; near_miss, after a deliberately almost-right change, must fail one; after_reset, after act_on_build_computer action reset, must give each check the result it had on the seed. Only a check that fails on what the app's view shows counts as failing: one that fails because the view could not be read or is cut short is undecided, and a stage only undecided checks would settle files nothing and is refused, to be checked again. A stage that does not hold, or after_reset, ends the witness: REA ends the recording and writes witness.json, the record as Evidence, with the recording's segments into directory, and returns the record.

inputs.name: stage

Never record one they did not give. The consent is kept with the computer; the export writes every one into the bundle's consent.json, and seeds withheld state only with a seed_sign_in consent.

inputs.name: subject

When neither confirms it, the error names what is left and the computer stays listed, so closing again retries. Closing cancels the call in progress on the computer and refuses those waiting for it.

inputs.name: computer_id

tools.name: recover_javascript_sources
tools.description: Recover readable modules from local UTF-8 JavaScript scripts/bundles into an absent directory, using caller-supplied Wakaru ^1.13.0 (verified with 1.14.0) on Linux x64. Use additional_paths for related chunks; each input retains its own snapshot and provenance. Returns original/derived digests, extraction byte ranges, emitted source maps, warnings and analysis_input inline. Structural splitting may fall back to one module; original names and runtime equivalence remain unknown. No application code execution. Requires util-linux prlimit; one worker, 1 GiB address-space ceiling, 120-second deadline, 64 MiB total input, 128 MiB output, 10000 entries and 8 MiB per diagnostic/report stream.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Absolute path to a UTF-8 JavaScript file; never executed

inputs.name: additional_paths
inputs.description: Additional absolute UTF-8 JavaScript files recovered together with path; each is snapshotted separately so imports can resolve across related chunks. All inputs share a 64 MiB total budget

inputs.name: output_directory
inputs.description: Absolute absent output directory; parent must exist

inputs.name: extraction_mode
inputs.description: Structural module boundaries, heuristic fallback, or finer inspection-only regions

inputs.name: rewrite_level
inputs.description: Upstream syntax recovery level; runtime equivalence remains unverified

tools.name: open_binary
tools.description: Open a local executable, application bundle, archive, JavaScript, source map, plist, or analysis database after validation. format=dos-com explicitly interprets 1..65280 headerless bytes as a DOS COM analysis image. format=raw-binary interprets headerless bytes with a required architecture and entry_point; file offset 0 maps at that address. Omission preserves header-based detection. provider_id selects one deep provider or deterministic auto selection; the binding remains stable until close or an explicit switch, with no failure fallback. Reopening the same target and profile retains its active database and metadata edits. Changing target or provider can retire the active Ghidra database and discard its ephemeral edits, including before a later provider call fails; retained investigation records are historical and do not restore those edits. For editable Ghidra persistence across processes, set REA_GHIDRA_CHECKPOINT_DIR to a private absolute directory in the startup environment (stock ELF/PE/Mach-O on Linux/macOS; restart MCP). Opens and normal close then restore/save automatically; no separate persistence tool or runtime setting update is needed. An optional analysis snapshot is imported atomically and must match the binary identity, concrete provider, and canonical analysis profile exactly; importing into a session with metadata mutations requires closing and reopening it first. Switching targets preserves investigation records. A failed admitted open reports error.details.selection_at_failure, target_at_open_completion, and provider_id_at_open_completion. The target summary and provider id are the selected binary and bound provider when that attempt settled, or null when absent. Later calls can change the selection, so use binary_session for current state. Call close_binary to release engine resources; reset_investigation explicitly clears investigation records.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Absolute local filesystem path for the analysis target; relative paths are rejected.

inputs.name: format
inputs.description: Explicit interpretation: dos-com or raw-binary (headerless), gamecube-dol (GameCube/Wii DOL, never auto-detected), or esp-flash-image (an ESP flash dump read with flash_offset and partition_table_offset). Omission preserves header-based detection.

inputs.name: architecture
inputs.description: Caller-supplied CPU family. Required with format=raw-binary; rejected otherwise. format=gamecube-dol takes powerpc from the header, so it must be omitted.

inputs.name: entry_point
inputs.description: Caller-supplied load and entry address (0xhex). File offset 0 is mapped here. Required with format=raw-binary; rejected otherwise. Optional with format=gamecube-dol; must equal the DOL header entry.

inputs.name: flash_offset
inputs.description: Flash address (0xhex) of the dump's first byte, when it does not start at flash address 0. Only with format=esp-flash-image.

inputs.name: partition_table_offset
inputs.description: Flash address (0xhex, a multiple of 0x1000) of the partition table, which disables the table scan. Only with format=esp-flash-image.

inputs.name: snapshot_path
inputs.description: Absolute local filesystem path for the analysis snapshot; relative paths are rejected.

tools.name: open_bundle_resources
tools.description: Open a local app bundle for read-only plist, Interface Builder, asset catalog, and keyed archive inspection without resolving or inventing its executable identity. This switches the shared session to a resource-only lane; executable analysis is unavailable until another target is opened.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Absolute local filesystem path for the analysis target; relative paths are rejected.

tools.name: close_binary
tools.description: Drain earlier requests and release the active engine, replay cache and owned resources while retaining investigation Evidence references and complete Unknown history in memory. Optionally save a target-bound analysis snapshot before closing; resource-only sessions have no binary snapshot binding. Later requests wait for this transition. Existing files require overwrite; a failed snapshot save keeps the engine open. Metadata edits prevent snapshot saves until the engine is recreated. Use reset_investigation to clear records explicitly, optionally saving a complete cross-domain Evidence bundle for import in a new process. With Ghidra checkpoint mode enabled, normal close saves Program metadata; a failed save retains the live Program for close retry. Closing does not automatically persist investigation Evidence/Unknown records.

inputs.name: snapshot_path
inputs.description: Absolute local filesystem path for the analysis snapshot; relative paths are rejected.

tools.name: reset_investigation
tools.description: Explicitly clear all retained Evidence and Unknown revision history, including engine replay/source bindings, while keeping a healthy active engine open. Drain earlier admitted work and queue later requests. Optional save_path writes the complete canonical Evidence bundle with file sync and atomic publication before clearing; import_evidence_bundle restores its original IDs and Unknown history in another process. Cancellation, save failure or incomplete cleanup preserves records; a published checkpoint remains reported on a later failure. Without save_path this discards in-memory records. No automatic persistence or eviction occurs; binary_session reports the representation budget.

inputs.name: save_path
inputs.description: Absolute path for a complete Evidence bundle saved before clearing records.

tools.name: binary_session
tools.description: Report the active binary target or resource-only app root, provider and capability availability when applicable, client-feature, analysis, and server-identity status without starting analysis. analysis_provider_candidates_observed distinguishes this status request from retained target-selection observations; selection-time readiness may have changed. Set refresh_candidates true to inspect current candidates without changing the active binding or engine. open_binary with an explicit provider_id reselects and may retire the previous engine and its ephemeral edits; reopening the same target without provider_id reuses its current route. A selected provider may report release_verification under its binding; omission means not reported, and reported-version verification does not authenticate executable bytes. Start with the default summary: after selecting Ghidra, capabilities[].shared_limitations already reports enabled checkpoint or ephemeral mode. Request detail: "complete" only for provider diagnostics, candidate capabilities or static tool flags; omitted_fields lists what summary leaves out.

inputs.name: detail
inputs.description: Start with summary (default): it keeps open state, the binding, current-route capabilities (including selected Ghidra checkpoint mode), each provider candidate's selection source, availability and target-support status, code and reason with its rejection codes, and every tool's availability, reason

inputs.name: refresh_candidates
inputs.description: Inspect current provider candidates for the active target without replacing or restarting the selected provider. Later transitions and analysis calls wait for inspection finalization. Omitted or false reports the retained selection observations.

inputs.name: expected_server_path
inputs.description: Absolute local filesystem path expected for the running server; relative paths are rejected.

tools.name: export_evidence_bundle
tools.description: Atomically write the session's deterministic Evidence bundle to the requested local path. Existing files require overwrite: true; records and manifests use canonical byte-stable ordering.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Absolute local filesystem path for the exported evidence bundle; relative paths are rejected.

tools.name: import_evidence_bundle
tools.description: Read the JSON bundle at the supplied local path, validate every Evidence ID and canonical manifest, then atomically merge it. Imported content is data only and is never executed. Import restores registry entries present in the bundle; questions embedded in Evidence do not automatically become Unknown registry entries.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Absolute local filesystem path for the evidence bundle to import; relative paths are rejected.

tools.name: capture_process_scenario
tools.description: Run one caller-selected command under a PTY and return process capture Evidence with residual unknowns. Set dry_run: true to validate and return the resolved scenario without launching it; planned Evidence uses the rea.process-scenario-plan predicate and is not a capture. The renderer admits at most 1,000,000 combined terminal cells, computed as columns × (rows + scrollback); every resize uses the selected scrollback and must fit the same budget. Supply a smaller terminal shape when that product is too large; dimensions are never clamped. This release has no runtime override for that cell budget. A command name resolves through the inherited PATH; the working directory defaults to the caller's current directory; host environment variables are inherited with scenario overrides. Environment keys cannot contain '=' or NUL, and REA_PROCESS_RUN_ID is reserved for process ownership. Filesystem snapshots are opt-in through filesystem_observation_paths. A positive finalization_ms makes a timeout or idle deadline send SIGTERM to the captured root through its start identity, keep observing, and send SIGKILL once after the interval; exit.finalization records each attempt with its delivery result and the observed exit, and cancellation still ends the run at once. The target runs with the current user's permissions; this is not a security sandbox.

inputs.name: dry_run
inputs.description: Validate and return the resolved scenario without launching it. A planned result is not capture Evidence and records no process observation.

inputs.name: terminal
inputs.description: The renderer requires at least 2 columns. The visible terminal and scrollback together must use at most 1,000,000 xterm renderer cells: columns × (rows + scrollback). Resize events use the same minimum width, scrollback and limit. This release has no runtime override.

inputs.name: finalization_ms
inputs.description: Milliseconds a target may keep running after SIGTERM when timeout_ms or idle_timeout_ms fires, before SIGKILL; 0 sends SIGKILL immediately. Both signals reach the captured root only while its launch-time start identity still matches; cancellation ends the run at once.

tools.name: compare_process_captures
tools.description: Compare two compatible process capture observations, supplied inline or as exact {kind: "retained-evidence", evidence_id} references from this session, across terminal, interaction, lifecycle, process, filesystem, command-shim, HTTP, and WebSocket evidence. Capture-local observer timing is retained as provenance but does not by itself establish a behavior change. Optional trace_spec validates exact events, including caller-selected timing assertions, against an explicit partial order or finite trace language; concurrency is never inferred from timestamps or broad sorting. Missing, journal-free, or truncated observations are never treated as equivalent.

tools.name: compare_artifacts
tools.description: Compare complete artifact inventories, including FIT and legacy uImage firmware components, by logical occurrence path, content identity, metadata, and graph relations. The root path . describes the outer container separately from its components. Name each side once without resending Evidence: {kind: "retained-evidence", evidence_id} selects an inspect_artifact result, its nested inventory, or its inspect_analysis_view summary retained in this session; {kind: "evidence-file", path, evidence_id?} reads one record from a local Evidence file or bundle at an absolute path. Complete inline Evidence is also accepted. Summary facts are not treated as a complete inventory; comparison resolves the exact complete parent from the same source bundle or the retained session. Every delta cites both complete inputs, and gaps yield truncated or unknown, never equivalence. Returns every change inline.

tools.name: match_native_functions
tools.description: Match two retained list_procedures inventories by unique exact reported symbols, then unique identical observed function bytes. Optional same-context list_names/procedure_info/read_bytes/analyze_function Evidence supplies symbol origin, exact bodies, bytes and dossier links as supplied static facts. Optional compatible CFG/call/string fingerprints from supplied dossiers propose unresolved groups only. Duplicate candidates remain unresolved groups; only_left/right mean unpaired within supplied observations, never proof of addition/removal. Default summary retains complete Evidence for filtered, selected-column, paged function-matches views. The byte-sources collection identifies selected read_bytes Evidence and its limitations; intersect its IDs with each function's evidence_links to identify its sources. Complete detail returns every group. Existing dossier pairs provide direct retained-reference compare_functions inputs.

inputs.name: left
inputs.description: Left list_procedures Evidence or exact retained reference

inputs.name: right
inputs.description: Right list_procedures Evidence or exact retained reference

tools.name: compare_functions
tools.description: Compare two explicit analyze_function Evidence records or exact retained session references across identity, exact provider text, calls, references, strings, and address-normalized CFG topology. The same authenticated Evidence record or compatible same-artifact entry coordinates establish correspondence independently of symbol origin; metadata and text changes remain separate. Missing or provider-incompatible facets remain truncated or unknown; every conclusion cites both Evidence sets.

tools.name: compare_bundles
tools.description: Compare two canonical Evidence bundles by exact record membership, explicit one-to-one observation pairs, and complete residual-unknown revision histories. Supply absolute local filesystem paths; relative paths are rejected. Missing bundle members describe omission only, never behavioral equivalence; output is digest-anchored and returns every change inline.

inputs.name: right_bundle_path

tools.name: find_changed_behavior
tools.description: Aggregate validated process, artifact, and function comparison Evidence, supplied inline or by exact retained-evidence references from this session. Original records and their complete source closure remain authenticated; summaries do not substitute for comparisons. Runtime observations remain distinct from static behavior candidates; missing or incomplete comparisons produce unresolved findings, never causal claims. Returns every finding inline.

tools.name: build_call_path
tools.description: Build every shortest direct-callee path from complete analyze_function Evidence supplied inline or by exact retained-evidence references. References reuse the complete parent of an analyze_function summary without resending dossiers. Uses exact canonical addresses; missing dossiers and provider mixing remain unknown, and every node and edge cites source Evidence.

tools.name: correlate_static_and_runtime
tools.description: Evaluate every explicit caller-declared hypothesis between static and runtime comparison Evidence supplied inline or by exact retained-evidence references. Similar names or paths are never auto-matched, consistent cochange never proves causality, and unknown or truncated inputs remain unresolved. Returns all correlations and their complete Evidence closure inline.

tools.name: verify_reconstruction
tools.description: Verify a finite typed behavioral and structural specification against a canonical Evidence bundle. Pass means every declared claim has complete comparable authority—not global source equivalence; changed claims fail and missing, limited, or unresolved evidence stays unknown.

tools.name: list_unknowns
tools.description: List current residual-unknown heads in deterministic ID order, with optional exact status, severity, and domain filters. Results are complete inline by default; supply offset and limit to page the filtered order. total is the matching-head count and next_offset is null when the page exhausts the result. This is read-only; unresolved, contradicted, and non-truth dispositions remain distinct. An empty registry does not mean retained Evidence has no residual questions; inspect the relevant Evidence or its analysis view.

inputs.name: offset
inputs.description: Zero-based offset in the stable filtered unknown ID order.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.description: Optional maximum number of heads to return. Omit to return every matching head from offset.

tools.name: record_unknown
tools.description: Create one deterministic residual unknown and immutable mutation evidence. Its scope is the active binary analysis target digest, or null without an active target; supporting Evidence does not select the scope. Scope contributes to stable identity. Validates all evidence and relationship references, and rejects duplicate stable identity.

tools.name: update_unknown
tools.description: Append one immutable full-state revision and mutation evidence. The unknown retains its original scope; the mutation Evidence subject is the active binary analysis target, or null without one, and can differ from that scope. Requires exact expected_revision; stale concurrent writers fail instead of overwriting newer analysis.

tools.name: verify_unknown_resolution
tools.description: Revalidate the current residual-unknown head against live bundled evidence, exact authority/confidence/environment requirements, and revision integrity. Withdrawn and out-of-scope dispositions are not truth claims.

tools.name: get_evidence_bundle
tools.description: Return every retained Evidence record and residual unknown as a complete canonical bundle by default. detail=summary discovers retained records without copying or transferring their payloads; optionally filter by exact Evidence ID, operation, target SHA-256, analysis-profile digest or canonical native procedure address. Metadata distinguishes complete record retention from native value-flow truncation or unavailable/unknown coverage. detail=records returns a page (offset, limit) of the matching complete records with unchanged IDs and their missing direct evidence_links; it is not an importable bundle. detail=links reads which evidence_links of the selected records this session or bundle retains, without their payloads: traversal retained-closure also follows retained links, the walk composed workflows require, and rows default to missing links. For supported parent operations, use a discovered evidence_id with a compatible inspect_analysis_view without restarting a provider. Filters apply to summary, records and links delivery.

inputs.name: offset
inputs.description: records or links: first matching row to return; default 0.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.description: records: maximum complete records, default 8. links: maximum link rows, default 64.

inputs.name: traversal
inputs.description: links only: direct (default) reads the selected records' own links; retained-closure also follows retained links.

inputs.name: link_status
inputs.description: links only: rows to return, default missing. Counts always cover every inspected link.

tools.name: get_navigation_context
tools.description: Return the selected document, current address, and containing/current procedure in one provider-neutral result. The result reflects sequential provider observations, not an atomic cursor snapshot; a cursor outside any procedure returns procedure: null.

tools.name: inspect_address_context
tools.description: Inspect one explicit reproducible address for its analyzed name, containing procedure, regular and inline comments, and matching bookmarks. Each unsupported facet returns a typed unavailable outcome. A facet rejected for invalid input, source Evidence integrity, or a resource constraint retains its canonical error and recovery alongside successful facets. Use xrefs, assembly, or pseudocode for those deeper views.

tools.name: list_cutter_sessions
tools.description: List live REA bridge sessions hosted by upstream Cutter instances, including observed document identity and bridge-directory security status. Discovery admits at most 256 descriptor candidates (16 MiB at the descriptor byte limit). That candidate budget is separate from REA_BRIDGE_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES and has no runtime override. Discovery reads and probes at most eight concurrently, and reports bridge_directory_capacity_exceeded rather than claiming no sessions when that budget is exceeded.

tools.name: cutter_command
tools.description: Run one arbitrary Rizin command in a selected live Cutter session. Commands may edit and persist analysis state or execute plugin-provided effects; completion uncertainty is returned as Evidence and must not be retried automatically. The authenticated request and response frame is bounded by REA_BRIDGE_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES (default 16777216 bytes, floor 7464, maximum 536870887). The payload budget excludes the terminating LF. An out-of-band Cutter process without the setting uses 16777216 bytes; a mismatch is refused before the command is sent. In a shared MCP server, this admitted command closes any active binary-analysis session; after its effects have settled, call open_binary before further analysis. Close an active Ghidra session explicitly first.

tools.name: inspect_with_objdump
tools.description: Run a caller-selected objdump command using GNU-style arguments against a local artifact, or request operation=architectures without a path to capture its response to -i. The executable implementation and version are not verified; other implementations may differ in options and output. For operation=disassemble, optional symbol selects native symbol-scoped disassembly before output collection; omission preserves all code sections. Matching and symbol boundaries follow the selected executable. Preserves decoded stdout and stderr inline with SHA-256 Evidence for artifact inspections, up to a shared 16 MiB combined limit; invalid UTF-8 bytes are represented by replacement characters and flagged in Evidence limitations. output_truncated reports output beyond that limit and completion_status is unknown if buffer enforcement terminated the process. The raw output is authoritative and REA does not claim a stable normalized format. DWARF does not follow local debug links by default. Set follow_debug_links to true to follow them; identities of external debug files are not bound to Evidence. REA clears DEBUGINFOD_URLS for objdump so DWARF processing does not make debuginfod network requests. Default detail complete returns original Evidence. Explicit detail summary retains the complete parent and returns its command observation once, without the raw mirror; parent_evidence_id supports later inspect_analysis_view summary queries and complete Evidence export. Architecture output is subjectless and does not establish support for any artifact. Optional command_timeout_ms is the per-phase wall clock in milliseconds (default 120000, range 1..2147483647); omitted means 120000 and the value applies on the next call. It does not raise the 16 MiB output cap.

inputs.name: command_timeout_ms
inputs.description: Wall-clock budget in milliseconds. Target preflight shares one budget across stat and digest, and the one-shot command receives that budget again (default 120000 each). Omitted means 120000. Applies on the next call. Does not raise the 16 MiB combined output cap, Ghidra or Hopper startup deadlines,

inputs.name: detail
inputs.description: complete returns the original Evidence; summary retains that complete parent and returns command output once with completion and source context.

inputs.name: symbol
inputs.description: Native symbol to disassemble, expressed as well-formed Unicode. Matching and symbol boundaries follow the selected executable; omitted means all code sections.

tools.name: execute_rizin_command
tools.description: Execute one caller-selected Rizin command against a local artifact using the Rizin CLI profile that suppresses user settings and scripts while retaining plugins. Preserves decoded stdout and stderr inline with SHA-256 Evidence, up to a shared 16 MiB combined limit; invalid UTF-8 bytes are represented by replacement characters and flagged in Evidence limitations. output_truncated reports output beyond that limit and completion_status is unknown if buffer enforcement terminated the process. Rizin commands and retained plugins can execute foreign code, mutate files, access the network, and read files outside the selected artifact; identities and contents of those external inputs are not bound to Evidence. Command effects depend on the Rizin command and loaded plugins; JSON is command-specific and raw output remains authoritative. For a raw image, asm_arch, asm_bits and asm_cpu select the decoder and base_address maps file offset 0 there; base_address also passes -n, which skips format loaders even for an ELF, and REA confirms neither. In a shared MCP server, this admitted command closes any active binary-analysis session; after its effects have settled, call open_binary before further analysis. Close an active Ghidra session explicitly first. Optional command_timeout_ms is the per-phase wall clock in milliseconds (default 120000, range 1..2147483647); omitted means 120000 and the value applies on the next call. It does not raise the 16 MiB output cap or a Rizin debugger session deadline.

inputs.name: asm_arch

inputs.name: asm_bits

inputs.name: asm_cpu

inputs.name: base_address
inputs.description: Address of file offset 0. REA passes -n and -m, so Rizin maps the file there as a raw image, reads no format headers, and keeps its default decoder unless asm_arch and asm_bits select one.

inputs.name: command_timeout_ms
inputs.description: Wall-clock budget in milliseconds. Target preflight shares one budget across stat and digest, and the one-shot command receives that budget again (default 120000 each). Omitted means 120000. Applies on the next call. Does not raise the 16 MiB combined output cap, Ghidra or Hopper startup deadlines,

tools.name: start_gdb_session
tools.description: Start a BYO GDB process in MI3 mode when available, suppress startup files, and disable auto-loading. Persistent GDB sessions are available only on Linux, where REA can verify live inferior output descriptors through /proc before detaching; macOS descriptor verification is not implemented, and Windows Job Object cleanup can terminate debugger inferiors. Optionally set inferior_tty to a caller-selected terminal for future inferior runs; REA verifies the setting through GDB/MI before the session becomes ready. The selected terminal must remain available after GDB exits. A live inferior can be detached during close only while this durable output sink remains verified. The session persists in this REA MCP server process and receives an explicit session ID.

inputs.name: inferior_tty
inputs.description: Caller-selected terminal path for future inferior runs. GDB must report the exact configured path before the session is ready.

tools.name: gdb_console
tools.description: Run one unrestricted GDB CLI command through MI interpreter-exec console and return raw MI, console, target, and log records inline with Evidence. Default detail complete preserves the original Evidence. Explicit detail summary retains that complete parent and returns every ordered MI record once, omitting duplicate stream groupings and raw mirrors; parent_evidence_id supports later inspect_analysis_view summary queries and complete Evidence export. A command timeout preserves collected records with completion_status unknown and stops the owned debugger session. Commands can execute shell, alter target state, access files, and use network. Closing the debugger never implies target termination. In a shared MCP server, this admitted command closes any active binary-analysis session; after its effects have settled, call open_binary before further analysis. Close an active Ghidra session explicitly first.

inputs.name: detail
inputs.description: complete returns the original Evidence; summary retains that complete parent and returns command output once with completion and source context.

tools.name: gdb_session_status
tools.description: Return the observed lifecycle state and bounded recent MI records and process diagnostics for one persistent REA GDB session; truncation and invalid-UTF-8 fields report discarded or lossy data.

tools.name: close_gdb_session
tools.description: Close the owned GDB process after verifying the inferior state. When one live thread group has a verified durable output TTY, REA automatically detaches it, which may resume target execution; otherwise close reports that a disposition is required. REA never kills attached or remote targets as part of debugger cleanup. In a shared MCP server, this admitted close retires any active binary-analysis session; after target effects have settled, call open_binary before further analysis. Close an active Ghidra session explicitly first.

tools.name: start_rizin_debug_session
tools.description: Start a persistent Rizin debugger session using `-N` to suppress user settings and scripts while retaining plugins, `-0` for NUL framing, and `-d` with an optional caller-selected IO debugger backend. Requires a caller-selected Linux TTY for inferior stdin, stdout and stderr; the target may read from and write directly to that terminal while running and after detach. Before detaching, REA verifies both output destinations, that the target does not hold the debugger command stream, and `dbg.exitkills=false`. Backend and target capabilities depend on the installed build. The session lives in this REA MCP process. Persistent sessions require Linux `/proc` descriptor readback. In a shared MCP server, starting this session retires any active binary-analysis session; after target effects have settled, call open_binary before further analysis. Close an active Ghidra session explicitly first.

tools.name: rizin_debug_command
tools.description: Execute one unrestricted command in a persistent Rizin debugger session. Returns raw output inline with Evidence, including backend output interleaved before the completion marker. If the command exceeds the output-byte, frame-byte, or frame-count limit, `output_truncated` is true and `completion_status` is `unknown`; retained partial output is returned and the owned debugger session is stopped. Evidence names the cap that stopped capture. Unsolicited frames already queued before the command make the session unavailable because correlation is ambiguous. Commands can access local files, shell, network, plugins, and target state; effects depend on the active backend and target. In a shared MCP server, this admitted command closes any active binary-analysis session; after its effects have settled, call open_binary before further analysis. Close an active Ghidra session explicitly first.

tools.name: rizin_debug_session_status
tools.description: Return observed lifecycle state and bounded recent NUL-framed output and process diagnostics for one Rizin debugger session; truncation fields report discarded data, and output_invalid_utf8 reports whether invalid UTF-8 has been observed in session frame bytes; recent output may contain replacement characters.

tools.name: close_rizin_debug_session
tools.description: Close the REA-owned Rizin debugger only after verifying no inferior remains or detaching one with a verified caller-selected TTY output sink. A detached target may continue running, read from and write to that TTY; target state is otherwise reported as unknown. REA never signals an inferior based on PID or path. In a shared MCP server, this admitted close retires any active binary-analysis session; after target effects have settled, call open_binary before further analysis. Close an active Ghidra session explicitly first.

tools.name: list_frida_devices
tools.description: List Frida devices currently available to this host, optionally connecting to the caller-selected remote Frida endpoint. Remote authentication options are used for this call only and are never returned or recorded.

tools.name: list_frida_processes
tools.description: List processes observed on a selected Frida device or caller-supplied remote endpoint. A remote connection is closed after discovery; authentication values are never returned or recorded.

tools.name: start_frida_session
tools.description: Attach Frida to one selected process or spawn one selected target. Spawned targets remain paused until resume_frida_session, allowing scripts to load before execution. Closing a session detaches instrumentation; it does not kill the target.

tools.name: load_frida_script
tools.description: Load caller-supplied JavaScript into a Frida session. Scripts can read or change target memory and behavior and can access the target process's capabilities. Messages and script errors are returned inline as Evidence; source content is not persisted.

tools.name: resume_frida_session
tools.description: Resume the process created by a paused Frida spawn session. Attached processes are already running and cannot be resumed through this operation.

tools.name: unload_frida_script
tools.description: Unload one caller-selected Frida script from a live session. This removes that script's instrumentation from the target.

tools.name: frida_session_status
tools.description: Read observed Frida session state on each call. Default detail=complete returns queued script messages and capture truncation. detail=summary retains the complete observation in this session and returns identity, state, scripts, retained message count and truncation without payloads. Export the complete parent with export_evidence_bundle; retained summaries are historical and never refresh live state.

tools.name: close_frida_session
tools.description: Unload session scripts and attempt to detach REA's Frida session. Then resume a still-paused spawned process if script cleanup or session detach confirms instrumentation was released. Cleanup failures are reported. REA never kills the target; its final state is reported as unknown.

tools.name: instrument_with_frida
tools.description: Run one caller-authored Frida script against an explicitly selected process and detach when the observation window ends. The CLI and MCP share this ephemeral workflow; use MCP session operations for persistent sessions. Remote authentication is used only for this call and excluded from Evidence.
